content: 1. A study published in the British Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in 1987 evaluated the policy of women maintaining their own obstetric records. The findings provided insights into the potential benefits and challenges of this approach. 2. The GRADE working group has developed a systematic framework for evaluating the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations in healthcare. 3. Grippo MLVS and Fracolli LA conducted an evaluation of an educational booklet designed to promote childcare from the perspective of family health and citizenship. This study was published in Revista da Escola de Enfermagem in 2008. 4. Hagiwara A, Ueyama M, Ramlawi A, and Sawada Y investigated the effectiveness of the Maternal and Child Health (MCH) handbook in improving health-related behaviors in Palestine. Their findings were published in the Journal of Public Health Policy in 2013. 5. Hamilton L and Wyver S explored parental use and perceptions of the child health personal record in Australia. Their research was published in Australian Educational and Developmental Psychology in 2012. 6. Harrison D, Heese H, Harker H, and Mann M assessed the Road-to-Health card based on the perceptions of clinic staff and mothers in South Africa. This study appeared in the South African Medical Journal in 1998. 7. Homer CSE, Davis GK, and Everitt LS introduced a woman-held record system in a hospital antenatal clinic as part of the Bring Your Own Records study. Their findings were published in the Australian and New Zealand Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in 1999. 8. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued recommendations on the use of home-based records for maternal, newborn, and child health, emphasizing their role in improving health outcomes. 9. Hully M and Hyne J examined the use of parent-held records in an oncology unit, with their findings published in Paediatric Nursing in 1993. 10. Hunter D, McCartney G, Fleming S, and Guy S explored the perspectives of residential care workers on promoting the health and well-being of children under their care. This study was published in Adoption & Fostering in 2008. 11. Kelly M, Hoonakker PLT, and Dean SM investigated the use of an inpatient portal to engage families in pediatric hospital care. Their findings were published in the Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association in 2017. 12. King G, Maxwell J, Karmali A, et al. studied the use, utility, and impact of a client/family health portal at a children’s rehabilitation hospital. Their research was published in the Journal of Medical Internet Research in 2017. 13. Kitayama K, Stockwell MS, Vawdrey DK, et al. explored parent perspectives on the design of a personal online pediatric immunization record. This study was published in Clinical Pediatrics in 2014. 14. Lakhani AD, Avery A, Gordon A, and Tait N evaluated a home-based health record booklet, with their findings published in Archives of Disease in Childhood in 1984. 15. Lee LK, Mulvaney-Day N, Berger AM, et al. developed the Patient Passport Program to improve communication between patients and providers for hospitalized minority children and their families. This study was published in Academic Pediatrics in 2016. 16. Lewin S, Booth A, Glenton C, et al. introduced the GRADE-CERQual approach for assessing the confidence in findings from qualitative evidence syntheses. This was published in Implementation Science in 2018. 17. Lovell A, Zander L, James CE, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess the effects of giving expectant mothers their own maternity case notes. This study was published in Paediatric and Perinatal Epidemiology in 1987. 18. Magwood O, Kpade V, Afza R, et al. systematically reviewed qualitative studies to understand the experiences of women, caregivers, and providers with home-based records. This work was submitted for publication in 2018. 19. Magwood O, Kpade V, Thavron K, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness of home-based records on maternal, newborn, and child health outcomes. This work was also submitted for publication in 2018. 20. Moore J, Brindle A, Goraya P, et al. developed a personal child health record for children with disabilities, with their findings published in Ambulatory Child Health in 2000. 21. Mori R, Yonemoto N, Noma H, et al. conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial on the Maternal and Child Health (MCH) handbook in Mongolia. This study was published in PLOS One in 2015. 22. O’Connor SO, Devlin AM, McGee-Lennon M, et al. examined factors affecting participation in the eRedBook, a personal child health record. Their findings were presented in Nursing Informatics in 2016. 23. Osaki K, Hattori T, Toda A, et al. conducted a cluster-randomized study in rural Java, Indonesia, to evaluate the use of the Maternal and Child Health handbook for maternal and child care. This study was published in the Journal of Public Health in 2018. 24. Phipps H explored the perspectives of pregnant women on carrying their own medical records. This study was published in the Australian and New Zealand Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in 2001. 25. Quinlivan JA, Lyons S, and Peterson RW surveyed pregnant women’s attitudes toward various medical record systems, including personally controlled electronic records. This study was published in Telemedicine and e-Health in 2014. 26. Sharp LK, Carvalho P, Southward M, et al. conducted an exploratory study on electronic personal health records for childhood cancer survivors. This study was published in the Journal of Adolescent and Young Adult Oncology in 2014. 27. Stille CJ, Christison-Lagay J, Bernstein BA, and Dworkin PH implemented a provider-based educational intervention to improve infant immunization rates. This controlled trial was published in Clinical Pediatrics in 2001. 28. Usman HR, Akhtar S, Habib F, et al. redesigned an immunization card and implemented center-based education to reduce childhood immunization dropouts in urban Pakistan. This randomized controlled trial was published in Vaccine in 2009. 29. Usman HR, Rahbar MH, Kristensen S, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to improve childhood immunization adherence in rural Pakistan through redesigned immunization cards and maternal education. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2011. 30. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed guidelines for the design, use, and evaluation of home-based maternal records, emphasizing their role in improving maternal, newborn, and child health outcomes. 31. WHO, UNICEF, and the World Bank Group collaborated on a framework for nurturing care to support early childhood development, aiming to transform health and human potential. This framework was published in 2018. 32. Yanagisawa S, Soyano A, Igarashi H, et al. evaluated the impact of a maternal and child health handbook on maternal knowledge and behavior in rural Cambodia. This community-based controlled trial was published in Health Policy and Planning in 2015. 33. Young SL, Gacic-Dobo M, and Brown DW conducted a survey of national immunization programs to assess home-based vaccination record practices in 2013. This study was published in International Health in 2015.
